Lookback context (pre-window): HN 2026-08-22 'Anthropic appears to be A/B testing reduced effort levels in Claude Code' (216 pts) and 2026-08-29/31 posts on weekly-limit reductions (25% from Sep 14) — corroborate existing K02/K07/D14; no new mechanism.
inferences: The deny-rule permission-guard cluster is a genuinely new mechanism class relative to the catalog: G17 covers chronic prompt fatigue and P-20260831-60EFB5BF covers false-ALLOW (checker interprets commands differently than the shell, letting side effects through); this cluster is the false-DENY dual — a conservative reachability over-approximation for file-access prediction that ignores the deny rule's own patterns and disables every auto-approval tier, making deny rules practically incompatible with autonomous/headless operation. Proposed as new candidate.

The Fable 5.1 / GPT-6 Astra quota-burn wave is materially K07 (rate limits interrupting work) amplified by K02 (model update changes behavior) and K06 (unpredictable token cost): the model update changed the consumption profile (output verbosity, cache accounting) with no quota re-calibration, so identical workflows went from sustainable to minutes-to-exhaustion overnight, across two vendors in the same week. Proposed as an update candidate on K07 (material_change=true) rather than a new problem.

The attribution-injection pattern is not represented in the catalog: H14 is the inverse (traceability missing), I06 covers secrets in prompts/logs, D03 covers instruction conflicts generally. The specific mechanism — harness-injected per-session directives that explicitly out-rank user configuration and write product metadata (session URLs) into public, hard-to-rewrite artifacts (git history, PRs) — is distinct and recurrent since June with a fresh in-window escalation (#92169 shows the override defeats explicit opt-out). Proposed as new candidate, medium confidence (community tier).
